title: Discovery of RNA and DNA viruses
author: Lily Tong
materials: To each pool add the following blocking reagents: A B 1 Component Volume (μl) 2 COT DNA 5 3 Salmon sperm DNA (1 mg/ml) 5 4 xGen Universal blockers 2 5 Total 12 NG SeqCap EZ Accessory Kit V2 Roche Catalog #7145594001 Salmon Sperm DNA Carrier Thermofisher Catalog #15632011 xGen Universal Blockers TS mix IDT Catalog #1075474

Prepare the wash buffers per capture as follows: A B C D E 1 Component Tube label Tube type Reagent volume (μl) Water volume (μl) 2 10x stringent wash buffer A PCR 20 180 3 10x stringent wash buffer B PCR 20 180 4 10x wash buffer 1 C PCR 10 90 5 10x wash buffer 1 D PCR 20 180 6 10x wash buffer 2 E PCR 20 180 7 10x wash buffer 3 F PCR 20 180 8 2.5x bead wash buffer G 1.5ml 200 300 SeqCap EZ Hybridization and Wash Kit Roche Catalog #5634253001

For each capture, place 100 µL, capture beads in a 1.5 mL tube. Can prepare the beads for up to six captures in a single tube. Equilibrate the capture beads to room temperature for 30 min and vortex for at least 15 sec before use. SEQCAP PURE CAPTURE BEAD KIT Roche Catalog #6977952001

Enrichment is performed with VirCapSeq-VERT probes and Roche SeqCap reagents. NG SeqCap EZ Accessory Kit V2 Roche Catalog #7145594001 SeqCap EZ Hybridization and Wash Kit Roche Catalog #5634253001 SEQCAP PURE CAPTURE BEAD KIT Roche Catalog #6977952001 VirCapSeq-VERT is no longer commercially available but we will soon release another version of this protocol with an alternative probe set.

steps.title: Prepare enrichment pools
steps.instruction: Combine 8–16 pre‑prepared Illumina metagenomic libraries so that each contributes equal ng of DNA, yielding a total of 1 µg DNA in a 1.5 mL LoBind tube; group samples by known viral load or, if unknown, by molarity or mass.

steps.title: Concentrate pool with beads
steps.instruction: Concentrate the pool using Agencourt AMPure XP beads (catalog #A63880) – ensure beads are at room temperature for 30 min and vortexed before use; alternatively use a speed‑vac if the volume is too high for bead cleanup.

steps.title: Add beads and blocking reagent
steps.instruction: Add 2 × the total volume of the pool together with the appropriate blocking reagent of the AMPure XP system.

steps.title: Separate beads on magnet
steps.instruction: Place the tube on a magnetic rack until beads and solution are fully separated (≈5 min).

steps.title: Remove supernatant
steps.instruction: Carefully pipette off the supernatant without disturbing the bead pellet.

steps.title: Ethanol wash beads
steps.instruction: Add 800 µL freshly prepared 80 % ethanol, incubate at room temperature for 1 min, then remove all ethanol traces without disturbing the beads.

steps.title: Air‑dry beads
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the bead pellet for ~3 min, taking care not to over‑dry.

steps.title: Prepare hybridisation mix
steps.instruction: Make a master hybridisation mix with 10 % excess: 7.5 µL 2× Hybridisation buffer, 3 µL Hybridisation component A (total 10.5 µL per sample) – reagents from SeqCap EZ Hybridization and Wash Kit (Roche catalog #5634253001).

steps.title: Add hybridisation mix
steps.instruction: Add 10.5 µL hybridisation mix directly to the bead‑bound DNA, remove the tube from the magnet and mix thoroughly; incubate at room temperature for 2 min.

steps.title: Elute into probe pool
steps.instruction: Place the tube back on the magnetic rack and transfer the entire 10.5 µL eluate into a new 0.2 mL PCR tube containing 4.5 µL VirCap‑VERT probe pool (use Applied Biosystems single‑cap PCR tubes, catalog N8010540). Mix by pipetting.

steps.title: First PCR incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate in a PCR machine with lid set to 105 °C: 95 °C for 5 min, then cool to 47 °C.

steps.title: Second PCR incubation
steps.instruction: Quickly transfer the tube to a second PCR machine with lid set to 57 °C and hold at 47 °C for 72 h.

steps.title: Equilibrate wash buffers
steps.instruction: Transfer tubes A and B (200 µL each of stringent wash buffer) and tube C (100 µL wash buffer 1) to the PCR machine to equilibrate them to 47 °C.

steps.title: Prepare capture beads
steps.instruction: Process the capture‑bead suspension as follows:

substeps.instruction: Place the bead tube on a magnet and remove liquid.
Add 2 × the initial bead volume of bead‑wash buffer (tube G).
Remove from magnet, vortex 10 s, then centrifuge briefly.
Place on magnet again and discard liquid (first wash).
Repeat the wash once more (total of two washes).
Resuspend beads in 1 × the original volume of bead‑wash buffer (tube G) by vortexing.
Transfer 100 µL of the resuspended beads to a fresh 0.2 mL PCR tube.
Place on magnet, remove liquid, and proceed immediately so beads do not dry.

steps.title: Hybridise probes to beads
steps.instruction: Immediately add 15 µL probe‑hybridisation sample to the prepared capture beads and pipette ten times to mix.

steps.title: Incubate probe‑bead mix
steps.instruction: Incubate in a PCR machine at 47 °C for 45 min with lid set to 57 °C; gently flick the tubes every 15 min to improve binding.

steps.title: First wash (buffer 1)
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL wash buffer 1 pre‑heated to 47 °C (tube C), vortex 10 s, place on magnet and discard liquid.

steps.title: Stringent washes
steps.instruction: Perform two stringent washes:

substeps.instruction: Add 200 µL stringent wash buffer pre‑heated to 47 °C (tube A), pipette 10 × to mix, incubate at 47 °C for 5 min.

steps.title: Transfer to LoBind tube
steps.instruction: Transfer the bead mixture to a fresh 1.5 mL LoBind tube; place on magnet and remove liquid.

steps.title: Wash with buffer 1 (RT)
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL wash buffer 1 at room temperature (tube D), vortex for 2 min, magnetise and discard liquid.

steps.title: Wash with buffer 2 (RT)
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL wash buffer 2 at room temperature (tube E), vortex for 1 min, magnetise and discard liquid.

steps.title: Wash with buffer 3 (RT)
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL wash buffer 3 at room temperature (tube F), vortex for 30 s, magnetise and discard liquid.

steps.title: Resuspend beads for PCR
steps.instruction: Remove the tube from the magnet, resuspend the beads in 20 µL nuclease‑free water, mix well by pipetting, and proceed directly to amplification (beads remain in solution).

steps.title: Prepare PCR mix
steps.instruction: Make a master PCR mix with 10 % excess: 25 µL 2× KAPA HiFi ready mix, 5 µL Post‑LM PCR oligos (total 30 µL per reaction) – reagents from SeqCap EZ Accessory Kit V2 (Roche catalog #7145594001).

steps.title: Aliquot PCR mix
steps.instruction: Dispense 15 µL PCR mix into each of two PCR tubes per capture sample.

steps.title: Add bead‑bound DNA
steps.instruction: Briefly vortex the bead‑bound captured DNA, spin down, then add 10 µL of this bead‑bound DNA to each PCR tube (beads stay in the reaction).

steps.title: Run on‑bead PCR
steps.instruction: Program the PCR machine: 95 °C 3 min; 14 cycles of 98 °C 20 s, 65 °C 15 s, 72 °C 30 s; final extension 72 °C 2 min; hold at 4 °C.

steps.title: Separate PCR beads
steps.instruction: Briefly centrifuge the PCR reactions, place tubes on a magnetic rack until beads and solution are fully separated.

steps.title: Combine PCR replicates
steps.instruction: Transfer 25 µL from each of the two PCR tubes into a fresh tube and combine them to obtain 50 µL per original pool.

steps.title: Cleanup and QC
steps.instruction: Clean up the pooled PCR products and perform quality control as described in the separate “Library clean‑up and quality control for Illumina sequencing” protocol.

steps.title: Calculate nM concentration
steps.instruction: Using fragment size (bp) and measured ng/µL, compute nM concentration: Conc (nM) = [sample (ng/µL)] ÷ [size (bp) × 660] × 1,000,000.

steps.title: Pool by equal molarity
steps.instruction: If multiple pools will be sequenced together, pool them at equal molarity, weighting each pool by the number of libraries it contains, as detailed in the “Library pooling and quality control for Illumina sequencing” protocol.

steps.title: Sequence on Illumina
steps.instruction: Sequence the final pools on an Illumina instrument following the manufacturer’s guidelines; target a depth of 20 million reads per sample (10 million for RNA viral discovery and 10 million for DNA viral discovery).
